about: Combustion (asta): a graha within a few degrees of the Sun is burnt and gives its own significations weakly. These rules fire only when the chart carries degrees, because combustion is a matter of longitude and cannot be read off house positions. The engine also weights every other rule about a burnt graha downward, so these statements name the condition rather than repeating its effect everywhere.

sources.locus: on the avasthas of the grahas and combustion

rules.says: The Moon is burnt: born within a day or so of the new moon, with a mind that runs quiet and a constitution that needs more rest than it admits.
Mars is burnt: the drive is there but spends itself on the wrong things, and physical stamina gives out sooner than the will does.
Mercury is burnt: quick but scattered, and the gap between what is understood and what comes out in words is wider than it looks from inside.
rules.note: Mercury is combust in roughly two charts out of five, simply because it never travels far from the Sun. It is the ordinary condition of Mercury rather than a misfortune, and most authorities weigh it lightly on its own.

rules.says: Jupiter is burnt: belief is held privately rather than taught, and the protection Jupiter usually gives arrives late or through someone else.

sources.locus: on the avasthas of the grahas and combustion

rules.says: Venus is burnt: affection is real but awkwardly expressed, and matters of marriage and comfort are delayed rather than denied.

sources.locus: on the avasthas of the grahas and combustion

rules.says: Saturn is burnt: endurance is undercut by the very authority it answers to, and relations with the father or with those in charge stay formal and cool.
